ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Lily pours 296 litres of water into the top of the pipework shown in the diagram. Each time a pipe forks, half the water flows to one side and half to the other. How many litres of water will reach container Y?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, water enters from the top vertical pipe opening, then the pipe first branches into two branches, left and right. The right-side branch goes downward along the right pipe and finally flows into the container labeled Y. The left-side branch continues downward and then branches once again, with one outlet flowing into the container labeled X and another outlet flowing into the container labeled Y. Reasoning: The total amount of water is 296 liters. The first branch splits equally, so the amount of water from the right branch flowing to Y is 296 ÷ 2 = 148 liters, and the left branch also has 148 liters. After the second branch of the left branch, half flows to Y, so this part is 148 ÷ 2 = 74 liters. Container Y receives a total of 148 + 74 = 222 liters. Final answer: 222 litres.

method.method_draft: Trace the pipe network from the diagram. Read from the image that the top entry first forks into a left branch and a right branch. The right branch ultimately empties into container Y. The left branch later forks again: one outlet goes to container X and the other outlet goes to container Y. Read from the text that 296 litres enter at the top and every fork splits the water equally. Compute: at the first fork, 296/2 = 148 litres go right to Y and 148 litres go left. At the second fork on the left side, half of 148, i.e. 74 litres, goes to Y. Therefore Y receives 148 + 74 = 222 litres.
